assumptions: PS1, PS2, PS3, S1, S2, and S3 are encoded as integer input variables used in guards because the NL calls them inputs and uses sensor/request conditions such as MU2 + S2; the reset signal is encoded as an event because it is a discrete global forcing signal.
hbrg is encoded as an integer output with 1 for upward drive, -1 for downward drive, and 0 for stopped floor states.

M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init verifies the initial transition lands on floor F1 with stopped hbrg, and with no requests the controller stays stopped at F1.
scenario_results.name: default_init_f1_no_request_stays_stopped

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes F1 request PS2 causing upward MU2 drive, then S2 arrival stopping at requested floor F2.
scenario_results.name: f1_ps2_moves_up_to_f2

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes F1 request PS3 causing upward MU3 drive, S3 arrival at F3, and reset forcing back to F1 from a floor state.
scenario_results.name: f1_ps3_moves_up_to_f3_then_reset

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes F2 request PS3 causing upward MU3 drive and S3 arrival stopping at F3.
scenario_results.name: f2_ps3_moves_up_to_f3

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes F2 request PS1 causing downward MD1 drive and S1 arrival stopping at F1.
scenario_results.name: f2_ps1_moves_down_to_f1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes F3 request PS1 causing downward MD1 drive and S1 arrival stopping at F1.
scenario_results.name: f3_ps1_moves_down_to_f1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes F3 request PS2 causing downward MD2 drive and S2 arrival stopping at F2.
scenario_results.name: f3_ps2_moves_down_to_f2

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes reset forcing F1 from a downward motion state, then from an upward motion state reached after the outstanding PS3 request context remains active.
scenario_results.name: reset_forces_f1_from_motion_contexts

evidence: NL requires floor states F1/F2/F3 and motion states MU2/MU3/MD1/MD2; DSL defines all seven leaf states.
NL transition examples are mirrored: F1->MU2 on PS2, F1->MU3 on PS3, F2->MU3 on PS3, F2->MD1 on PS1, F3->MD1 on PS1, F3->MD2 on PS2, MU2->F2 on S2, MU3->F3 on S3, MD1->F1 on S1, MD2->F2 on S2.
DSL enter actions set hbrg=1 for MU2/MU3, hbrg=-1 for MD1/MD2, and hbrg=0 for F1/F2/F3.
DSL includes [*] -> F1 and ! * -> F1 :: reset.
findings.summary: The DSL is faithful to the explicit NL elevator controller requirements: all named floor and motion states, request-triggered motion transitions, arrival-sensor transitions, hbrg drive/stop outputs, initial F1 state, and global reset-to-F1 behavior are represented.

evidence: inspect_model_to_json_summary reports 7 leaf states, 11 normal transitions, 7 forced reset transitions, 7 variables, 1 event, and 7 actions.
GroundingMap contains required entries for states, variables, hbrg actions, request transitions, sensor arrival transitions, and reset.
sim_summary reports 8 scenarios passed out of 8, including all named request-to-motion and arrival paths plus reset behavior.
findings.summary: Core finite-state-machine components are covered, including states, variables, events, transition guards, and output actions. The model is not an empty-shell DSL and appears to be a T3 strong reviewed candidate within the supplied review boundary.

evidence: DSL has competing guards from F1 when PS2 > 0 and PS3 > 0 are both true.
DSL has competing guards from F2 when PS1 > 0 and PS3 > 0 are both true.
DSL has competing guards from F3 when PS1 > 0 and PS2 > 0 are both true.
sim_summary scenario samples use one request target at a time and do not show concurrent PS inputs.
findings.summary: The simulations focus on single active request/sensor cases and do not exercise ambiguous simultaneous request conditions where multiple outgoing guards from a floor state may be true at once.

evidence: From F1, both F1 -> MU2 if [PS2 > 0] and F1 -> MU3 if [PS3 > 0] can be enabled together.
From F2, both F2 -> MU3 if [PS3 > 0] and F2 -> MD1 if [PS1 > 0] can be enabled together.
From F3, both F3 -> MD1 if [PS1 > 0] and F3 -> MD2 if [PS2 > 0] can be enabled together.
findings.summary: The controller permits nondeterministic or implementation-order-dependent behavior under simultaneous requests because no priority, mutual exclusion, or arbitration guard is modeled. This is advisory because the NL does not explicitly define concurrent-request arbitration.

evidence: NL only requires PS1/PS2/PS3 as floor-request inputs and S1/S2/S3 as arrival sensing inputs.
design_diagnostics_summary identifies PS1/PS2/PS3/S1/S2/S3 as nl_external_input_vars.
No NL requirement states that requests must be cleared after arrival or that queued requests must be stored internally.
findings.summary: The model intentionally represents requests and sensors as external input variables and does not model request clearing, call queues, door timing, or physical intermediate floor traversal. These omissions are acceptable for the supplied NL, which specifies a compact FSM over named floor and motion states.

evidence: DSL includes ! * -> F1 :: reset.
F1 enter action sets hbrg = 0.
sim_summary includes reset_from_f3_forces_f1 and reset_forces_f1_from_motion_contexts passing.
findings.summary: No unsafe recovery issue is identified. Reset behavior is globally modeled and returns to F1 while stopped, matching the NL statement that reset forces the controller back to floor 1 regardless of outstanding request context.

evidence: design_diagnostics_summary reports blocking_count 0 and advisory_count 17.
external_input_role_ledger marks PS1, PS2, PS3, S1, S2, and S3 as external_input_candidate.
GroundingMap assumptions state that request and sensing variables are encoded as integer input variables.
findings.summary: No unjustified warning repair is evident. The advisory unwritten-read and guard-vars-never-change diagnostics are consistent with externally driven request and sensor inputs rather than an unsupported local repair.

evidence: Required states, transitions, guards, reset, and hbrg output actions are present.
design_diagnostics_summary ok is true with no blocking diagnostics.
sim_summary ok is true with 8/8 scenarios passed.
The DSL is not an empty shell: action_count is 7 and transition_count is 18 including forced reset expansions.
findings.summary: No NFRR quality cap is warranted. The model has substantive grounded state/transition/action coverage and passes the supplied simulations; estimated tier is T3 strong reviewed candidate, not T0/T1.
